title: Mixing forcing names and choosing witnesses

based_on.title: The maximum principle in forcing and the axiom of choice

summary: Splice an antichain of ground names into one witness at the original forcing condition, keeping the ground choices explicit.
abstract: A forcing condition may guarantee that a witness exists even though different generic extensions give different witnesses. Names can accommodate this variation: incompatible conditions may select different values of one fixed name. We construct that name from an antichain of local choices and prove that its value is exactly the chosen branch’s value. In a transitive ground model of ZFC, Collection and Choice assemble the local witnesses into a ground family. The resulting maximum principle chooses one ground name that works at the original condition, without any chain-condition assumption.
